courses.subject: GEYS
courses.title: Social Responsibility through Community Engagement
courses.description:
Service-learning nurtures social responsibility by encouraging students to recognize community needs and commit to contributing positively to society. Key concepts related to sustainable development from different perspectives, such as health and well-being, quality education, reducing social inequality, and sustainable cities and communities, will be explored.
This course introduces the concepts and principles of service-learning, as well as approaches of conducting needs assessment, programme design and implementation. Students will form groups to study their assigned service targets, including but not limited to ethnic minorities, children with special educational needs, the elderly, and primary school students. Students will then communicate with the designated NGOs, design and implement a 13-hour service-learning project.
Upon completion, students will reflect on their projects and learning experiences. By the end of the course, students will be able to identify ways to address community issues and recognize the value of personal involvement in the community for socially constructive purposes.

courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing this course, the student will be able to:

1. understand key concepts related to sustainable development from different perspectives, such as health and well-being, quality education, social inequality, and sustainable cities and communities

2. identify ways to address community issues

3. connect classroom learning with personal experience

4. recognize the value of personal involvement in community for socially constructive purposes, and demonstrate social responsibility

5. work and communicate effectively in a team work environment
courses.course_syllabus:
Service-learning nurtures social responsibility by encouraging students to recognize community needs and commit to contributing positively to society. Key concepts related to sustainable development from different perspectives, such as health and well-being, quality education, reducing social inequality, and sustainable cities and communities, will be explored.

This course then engages students to identify a social problem and design a service programme to address the needs of the service users. Students will form groups to design and implement 13-hour service-learning activities. Students will then reflect upon their project after the service, so that they can learn from first-hand experience the root of the concerned social issues and ways to address these issues.

Class Schedule and Contents:

Week 1: Course Introduction and Theory

Week 2: NGO Pre-service Training and Service Design Discussion

Week 3: Proposal Submission and Consultation

Week 4 - 10: Service Implementation (4 – 6 sessions of service will be arranged, each of 2 – 3 hours)

Week 11 - 12: Group Presentation
